name: session_question_score
description: FR-BB311 -- ports session_question_scores from c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\BilimBaga\backend\migrations\016_session_question_scores.up.sql. Product spec: corporate_exam_platform_roadmap.md section 3.6. FIELD-LEVEL NOTES. session_id is :string, queried: true, required: true, foreign_keys entry fk_session_question_score_session_id against session. question_id is :string, queried: true, required: true, foreign_keys entry fk_session_question_score_question_id against question. score is :decimal with decimal_precision 6 and decimal_scale 4, ported verbatim from the source's DECIMAL(6,4), queried: false, required: true (source DEFAULT 0). max_score is :decimal with decimal_precision 6 and decimal_scale 4, same source type, queried: false, required: true (source DEFAULT 1). grading_status is :enum with values graded, pending_manual, ai_graded, queried: true, required: true (source DEFAULT 'graded'). CONSTRAINT: constraints entry uq_session_question_score_session_id_question_id, type unique, over (session_id, question_id) -- this expresses the source's composite PRIMARY KEY (session_id, question_id) without declaring a primary key, because the record subsystem owns record identity; the same convention session_question and session_answer follow above. INDEX: idx_session_question_score_session_grading_status over (session_id, grading_status) stands in for the source's partial index idx_session_question_scores_pending ON session_question_scores(session_id) WHERE grading_status = 'pending_manual' -- Letflow's index_def has no WHERE clause, so this is a FULL composite index over every grading_status value, not a partial index limited to pending_manual rows; it is a difference, not an equivalent, though it still serves the same query shape (find a session's pending-manual rows) at the cost of indexing the other two statuses as well. ON DELETE: session_id's FK is CASCADE in the source and RESTRICT in Letflow (ddl.ex:675, decision 0025) -- a divergence; question_id's FK is RESTRICT in the source already, so Letflow's fixed RESTRICT matches. Both rows are in the seven-row table in README-constraints.md. OMISSIONS. No id, created_at or updated_at field is declared, for the usual cross-subsystem reason -- the source table in fact has no id or timestamp columns of its own either, only the composite PK. No created_by field is declared -- grading is attributable via the event stream's actor_id on whichever record write applied it (manual grading or the AI grading pipeline), not a column on this row. ANALYTICS FIELDS (REQ-594): exam_id is :string and correct is :boolean, both queried: true and required: false, additive and optional, written by the score writer (REQ-594 part B); rows written before carry neither. This entity type has no datetime column, so the TIMESTAMPTZ divergence recorded in README-constraints.md does not apply here.
